+# --- the predictions section: ONE parser, two callers --------------------------

+# gate — it is exactly the defect retro 2026-07-29 D1 diagnosed: the launch gate

+# tenant project's first wave scored `unpredicted` with no error printed anywhere,
+# and the wave brief recorded 6/6 against an actual 4 of 6.

+# THE FOUR LABELS ARE LITERAL. They are pinned verbatim by the design-partner
+# authoring rules (seats/design-partner/PROTOCOL.md); re-wording one does not
+# degrade the score, it erases it. They are printed on every refusal, so an author
+# who tripped the gate reads the answer instead of guessing at it.

+# THREE OF THE FOUR ARE SCORED. `- Named risks:` is required by the authoring
+# protocol, written by every author, and read by no instrument — this parser does
+# not extract it and `hive-score` does not score it. That is said out loud here
+# and in the refusal text rather than quietly repaired: newly scoring a field
+# changes the contents of a launch gate, and gate contents are the operator's to
+# change, not the tooling's (retro 2026-07-29 R9, held at operator review).
+#
+# Consumed by the sourcing scripts (hive-launch's refusal text), not within this file.
+# shellcheck disable=SC2034

+  - Expected questions: <count or range> — <named seams, or a designed round-trip>
+  - Expected review outcome: <clean | minor rework | rework> — <why>
+  - Named risks: <what could turn the shape of the work>'

+  three above are what `hive-score` parses.'

+# predictions: "one line declaring the task deliberately unpredicted and why".
+# The declaration is a literal too, for the same reason the labels are — a phrase
+# only a human can recognise is not a disposition an instrument can honour.

+# parse_predictions <order-file> — sets, always, never dies:
+#   PRED_SECTION      1 if the file carries a `## Predictions` heading, else 0
+#   PRED_BLOCK        the section body, verbatim (empty if no section)
+#   PRED_DECLARED     1 if the section declares the task deliberately unpredicted

+#                     verbatim prediction slices; empty when that field did not
+#                     parse (a no-match is the expected partial case, not an error)
+#   PRED_FIELDS       how many of the three parsed (0-3)
+#   PRED_MISSING      comma-separated names of the ones that did not

+# the order exists check that themselves, and they have better messages for it.

+  if grep -qE '^##[[:space:]]*Predictions[[:space:]]*$' "$file"; then PRED_SECTION=1; fi
+  [ "$PRED_SECTION" -eq 1 ] || return 0
+
+  # From the `## Predictions` heading to the next heading of any level, exclusive.

+    /^##[ \t]*Predictions[ \t]*$/ { inblock = 1; next }
+    inblock && /^#/                { inblock = 0 }

+  ' "$file")

+  # `|| true` throughout: a no-match grep exits 1, and under `set -o pipefail`
+  # that would abort the caller on the ordinary partial-prediction case.

+    | grep -oiE 'Expected effort:[[:space:]]*[0-9][0-9.–—-]*[[:space:]]*worker-hours?' \

+    | grep -oiE 'Expected questions:[[:space:]]*[0-9][0-9–—-]*' \
+    | head -1 | sed -E 's/^[Ee]xpected questions:[[:space:]]*//'; } || true )

+    | grep -oiE 'Expected review outcome:[[:space:]]*[^.]+' \
+    | head -1 | sed -E 's/^[Ee]xpected review outcome:[[:space:]]*//'; } || true )

+  # Coverage, and which fields were lost — "1 of 3" without naming the two is a
+  # number an author cannot act on.

+  # A here-string, not `printf | grep -q`: `-q` exits at the first match and the

+  # shellcheck disable=SC2034  # read by the callers (hive-launch's gate, hive-score's coverage)
+  if grep -qiF -- "$PREDICTION_UNPREDICTED_DECL" <<<"$PRED_BLOCK"; then PRED_DECLARED=1; fi

-    if ! git -C "$OPS_WS" pull --rebase --quiet; then
-      echo "hive: push failed and rebase failed — committed locally in $OPS_WS, NOT on the hub; resolve by hand" >&2
-      return 1
-    fi
-    git -C "$OPS_WS" push --quiet \
-      || { echo "hive: push failed for $OPS_WS — committed locally, NOT on the hub" >&2; return 1; }
+    {

+### The drill-hygiene sweep (order scope 7 — bounded to two named classes)
+

+**Class A — EXIT trap installed before the isolation it depends on: none found.** The class is
+real and expensive (`launch-pane-fix` shipped one where `cleanup`'s `tmux kill-server` would
+have reached the operator's live server), but it has no target here. `hive-metrics-drill.sh`'s
+`cleanup` has exactly one side effect, `rm -rf "$SANDBOX"`; `SANDBOX` is assigned at line 18 by
+`mktemp -d` and the trap is installed at line 54, so the value and the directory both exist
+before the trap can fire, and a failed `mktemp` aborts under `set -e` while no trap is
+installed. There is no `kill-server`, no container command, and no push to a shared remote in
+its cleanup — nothing whose blast radius depends on an isolation step. Stated rather than left
+silent, because "we looked and there is nothing" is the finding.
+
+**Class B — `cmd | grep -q` under `set -o pipefail`: three instances found, all three fixed.**
+The drill's three stop-line assertions:
+
+```bash
+check "hive-metrics contains no emit" "! code '$M' | grep -Eq '…emit…'"
+check "hive-score contains no emit"   "! code '$S' | grep -Eq '…emit…'"
+check "neither tool commits to git"   "! { code '$M'; code '$S'; } | grep -Eq 'git .*(commit|push)'"
+```
+
+`grep -q` exits at the first match and SIGPIPEs its upstream, which fails the pipeline under
+`pipefail`. What makes these worse than the `cli-qol` instance is the negation: `cli-qol`'s bug
+produced a false **FAIL** against a correct repository — loud, and it got found. These produce a
+false **PASS**, and they are the three assertions that certify the read-only stop-line the order
+itself names. "hive-score issues no events" going green *because the check broke* is the worst
+failure this file can have.
+
+They are **latent today, not live**: the upstream is a whole-file `grep -v` whose output
+(~15 KB and ~9 KB) still fits in a 64 KB pipe buffer, so every write completes before `grep -q`
+can close the read end and no SIGPIPE is delivered. That is a size, not an invariant —
+`hive-metrics` is 28 KB and growing. Fixed by reading the stripped source into variables once
+and matching with here-strings, so no pipeline exists to break.
+
+Two further Class-B *near*-instances were considered and deliberately left: `printf '%s' "$VAR"
+| grep -q` (roughly twenty sites) and `entry <task> | grep -q`. Their upstreams are a shell
+builtin and a small `awk`, both bounded by construction and far below the buffer, and — the
+reason it is safe to leave them — nearly all are positive assertions, where a spurious pipeline
+failure is a loud false FAIL rather than a silent false PASS. Churning twenty lines to no effect
+is not what the order asked for. The **new** code added by this task uses here-strings
+throughout, so the count does not grow.

+## Reflection
+
+**The gate needed a literal for "deliberately unpredicted", and I had to choose it.** The
+authoring protocol offers the escape hatch as "one line declaring the task deliberately
+unpredicted and why" — prose, which is precisely the surface D1 proved does not bind. An
+instrument cannot honour a disposition only a human can recognise, so the parser matches the
+literal phrase `deliberately unpredicted` (case-insensitive, anywhere in the section). That is a
+new literal in the authoring contract, and it belongs in
+`seats/design-partner/PROTOCOL.md` next to the four labels — a design-partner edit, not a
+worker's, so it is named here rather than made. Until it lands, the refusal message itself
+teaches the phrase, which is the same reason the four labels are printed there.
+
+**One coverage string the order did not ask for.** The order requires two strings, absent and
+unparsed. I added a third for the declared case. The reasoning is the order's own: recording a
+deliberately-unpredicted order as "section present, 0 of 3 fields parsed" would tell a reader
+the instrument lost a prediction that was never made — a fresh instance of exactly the lie D1
+was. It is a coverage string, not a scored field, so no stop-line is touched; but it is scope I
+took, and reverting it costs only the honesty of one row.
+
+**The interesting question was where the gate goes, not what it checks.** The order says "before
+any spine write". The stronger placement is before the *WIP throttle*, which is where I put it:
+a launch that would refuse on predictions should say so even when review debt would also have
+refused it, because the author can act on the labels and cannot act on someone else's review
+backlog. It also means the refusal costs nothing at all — no board read, no clone, no tmux.
+
+**Effort was consumed by the drills, not the tools.** The six behaviour changes are ~250 changed
+lines across four scripts, most of it the comments that say why; the logic is small. The 36 new metrics-drill assertions, the
+two new fixture tasks, and the mutation testing are most of the diff and nearly all of the time
+— then the tooling-drill cases, which are written blind because they cannot be run here. I have
+no clock to quote; the branch's commit timestamps are the only number I can point at.
+
+**A methodology note that cost me the work once.** I ran a mutation test whose cleanup was
+`git checkout -- scripts/` while the implementation was still uncommitted, and lost every change
+in this task's scope. Rebuilt from the session's own record, then committed *before* resuming
+the mutation runs. If a future worker takes one thing from this report: commit before you
+deliberately corrupt your own tree, and prefer a temporary copy to `git checkout` as the
+restore step.
+
+**On the two third-class drill findings.** Both are one-line fixes and I left both alone,
+because the order pre-decided that a third class is a finding rather than a fix, and a
+bounded sweep whose boundary moves whenever the worker finds something tempting is not a
+bounded sweep. Finding 1 in particular deserves a carrier: it is the failure mode where a
+harness lies in the reassuring direction, which is the same class as D1 itself and as
+stall-ledger S3 — a green-looking silence covering a thing that did not run. If a third
+harness-held defect is the ledger's trigger for machinery, this is a candidate for being it.
